Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:25: One must also consider and know that according to the path through which each thing was created, so its aspect and form indicates. Like the rose, which has thirteen petals and five sturdy leaves, as Rashbi, of blessed memory, explains (Zohar, Bereishit 1a): one must understand and consider the divine wisdom that created it through the power of a particular path, and therefore its production is obligated to have that number of petals. And there is a rose that has five petals, as is explained in the Tikkunim (71a), indicating the five letters of Elohim, as Rashbi explains there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:26: Along these lines, concerning the candle, Rashbi explains (Zohar, Bereishit 50b) that it indicates the secret of supernal union - his words: "but come and see, whoever wishes to know the wisdom of holy union should observe the flame rising from a coal or from a burning lamp," etc.; and he explains there that the rising flame, white light, hints at Tiferet, and the coal, which has the color of blue-black, corresponds to the Shechinah, which is fire. At the end of his words I found, in manuscript, a pleasant matter - his words: "and upon the white light rests above a concealed light that encompasses it, and here is a supernal secret" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:27: Along these lines is the matter of fish, which have no covering over the eye, indicating the place of their supernal hint, which is an open eye, as is explained in the Idra of Naso (Zohar 129b), see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:28: Likewise, the black rooster that crows at midnight to awaken people to the service of the Creator - its matter is explained there (Vayechi 218a), and we quoted its words in the Gate of Fear, chapter 12, see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:29: Along these lines, for other things in the world, one must discern the secret of supernal wisdom within them; and so Rashbi explains (Shemot 15a) - his words: Rabbi Akiva said to him, this implies that everything the Holy One, blessed be He, does is to learn from it abundant wisdom, as it is said (Proverbs 16:4) "the Lord has made everything for its purpose." Rabbi Elazar said, [we derive this] from here, as it is written (Genesis 1:31) "and God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very [me'od] good" - what is "me'od"? To learn from it abundant supernal wisdom. Rabbi Yehudah said, what is meant by (Ecclesiastes 7:14) "God has made this one alongside that one"? In the pattern of the firmament, the Holy One, blessed be He, made [things] on earth, and all of them hint at what is above - so far, as relevant to us. There they explain the kinds of fruits and trees, their hints, such as the walnut, which has four parts, hinting at the four sources of rivers, which are the secret of the Chariot, and the rest may be examined there; to avoid lengthening, we have not quoted all his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:30: Along these lines, the discerning reader must observe the whole account of Creation and give a bond and cause between each cause and its effect, and thereby know and recognize that there is one Creator of all, and all were given by one Shepherd. Especially when he further knows that the account of Creation is expounded both above and below - above, in the supernal spiritual beings, and below, in this world. This is [the meaning of] "Bereishit" - two "reishit"s [beginnings], a beginning above and a beginning below, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:31: We find, then, that this world, although it took on physical form below, has spirituality above in its generalities and particulars; and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Beshalach 48b) - his words: "come and see, the pattern above exists below; the pattern below exists in the sea; the pattern above exists above, in the supernal sea; the pattern above exists below, the pattern below exists in the lower sea. The body of that sea - we have already established for our colleagues - its length and width, head and arms, hairs and body, all as needed, and all is called by its Name; and in this pattern below, in the lower sea, likewise the head of the sea and the arms of the sea and the body of the sea" - so far. Rashbi explains something similar (Shemot 20a), which we have not quoted, to avoid lengthening.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:32: The reason it is necessarily so, that everything above has a corresponding counterpart below, is that existing things are like a seal stamped one from another, down to these physical things - first Adam of Atzilut, the totality of existing things in their fineness, stamped in Adam of Beriah, and so from Beriah to Yetzirah and Asiyah. Therefore it is necessarily so that in Asiyah there be an image of Adam, and therefore it says that the sea has hairs and arms.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:33: Along these lines, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Pekudei 231b) that in the making of the Tabernacle there was the same pattern as the making of heaven and earth, and likewise the lower Garden of Eden is a seal of the upper world and the lower world - his words: "it is written, 'in the beginning God created the heavens and the earth,' and they have established that everything was made this way in the pattern of the Tabernacle - the pattern of the lower world He made, and the pattern of the upper world, and all His works that He made in the pattern above - so too the Tabernacle, all its works are like the pattern of the upper world; this secret - all the works of the Tabernacle are all works and repairs of above and below, in order to make the Shechinah dwell in the world in supernal dwellings and lower dwellings; in this manner, in the Garden of Eden below is the pattern above and the pattern below - all the forms and all the images of the world, all are there" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:34: Included in this, we understand that the measurements of the making of the Temple were all made with a supernal design, to hint at the measurements of the supernal Temple, as is written in Chronicles (I Chronicles 28:11) "and David gave Solomon his son the plan of the porch and its houses, its treasuries and its upper chambers and its inner rooms," etc. (ibid. 28:19) "all this, said David, the Lord made me understand in writing, by His hand upon me, all the works of this plan." We find, then, that all these existing things are the pattern of these, the lower ones being the image and pattern of the upper ones.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:35: Along these lines, our Sages, of blessed memory, explain that the earth has an entire human countenance - their words (Midrash Zuta, Kohelet 1:4): "'and the earth abides forever' (Ecclesiastes 1:4) - Reish Lakish said, everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created in man, He created in the earth. Man has a head, and the earth has a head, as it is said (Proverbs 8:26) 'and the head [rosh] of the dust of the world.' Man has eyes, and the earth has eyes, as it is said (Exodus 10:15) 'and it covered the eye of all the earth.' Man has ears, and the earth has ears, as it is said (Isaiah 1:2) 'and give ear, O earth.' Man eats, and the earth eats, as it is said (Numbers 13:33) 'a land that devours its inhabitants.' Man drinks, and the earth drinks, as it is said (Deuteronomy 11:11) 'it drinks water from the rain of heaven.' Man is agitated, and the earth is agitated, as it is said (II Samuel 22:8) 'then the earth shook and quaked.' Man becomes drunk, and the earth becomes drunk, as it is said (Isaiah 24:20) 'the earth staggers like a drunkard.' Man vomits, and the earth vomits, as it is said (Leviticus 18:25) 'and the land vomits out its inhabitants.' Man has hands, and so the earth, as it is said (Genesis 34:21) 'and the land is wide-handed.' Man has a navel, and so the earth, as it is said (Ezekiel 38:12) 'who dwells at the navel of the earth.' Man has thighs, and so the earth, as it is said (Jeremiah 31:7) 'and I will gather them from the sides [thighs] of the earth.' Man has feet, and so the earth, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 1:4) 'and the earth abides forever' and stands at its post" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:36: Along these lines, our Sages, of blessed memory, explain, quoted in the Yalkut (Psalms, siman 672), at the beginning of the psalm "the heavens declare" (Psalms 19:1-2), that the sea and the heavens have [limbs], and although not all are mentioned, they hint at all the limbs: they say that the sea has eyes, as it is said (Psalms 114:3) "the sea saw and fled," and it has hands, as it is said (ibid. 104:25) "this sea, great and wide of hands"; and the heavens have a heart, as it is said (Deuteronomy 4:32) "to the heart of the heavens," and likewise the sea, as it is said (Exodus 15:8) "the depths froze in the heart of the sea." The heavens have a mouth, as it is said (Psalms 19:2) "the heavens declare," and likewise the earth, as it is said (Numbers 16:32) "and the earth opened its mouth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:37: Regarding all these limbs mentioned in the sea, heavens, and earth, it says in the midrash (Yalkut, there) that they are not visible to creatures but only before the Holy One, blessed be He, and we must say that this is the reality of the spiritual account, which is not grasped by the lower human beings, but in the reality of its spirituality there is a hint of the limbs mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:38: Rabbi Yosef Gikatilla, peace be upon him, writes in his commentary on Ezekiel's Chariot a pleasant matter concerning examination; I have chosen to quote his words, peace be upon him - his words: "and behold, the Name, blessed be He, since He created the angels in ultimate perfection and inwardness, although we cannot make visible to the sensory eye the hidden forms, the form of the stars is shown, to understand from within them the forms that are hidden. And behold, the sun and moon, both are clear witnesses that show us the supernal hidden things, hidden and concealed in the secrets of the supernal Chariots; and this is the secret of (Genesis 1:16) 'and God made the two great lights' - truly great lights they were, to illuminate the earth, to enlighten the eyes of us who dwell on earth, to understand from within them the secret of several supernal hidden things, in the order of the intellectual levels, and above, in the secret of the sefirot, and in the secret of the reality of the Name, blessed be He, and His unity. And behold, all the arrangements, supernal and lower, hidden and revealed, are all analogues to the secrets of the supernal Chariot, and from the sensory and grasped things we can understand and know those hidden and concealed things - this is the secret of (Isaiah 40:26) 'lift up your eyes on high and see who created these'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:39: He further writes, on the matter of "the likeness of a man" mentioned there, that all the arrangements of the Chariot are all arranged in the pattern of the form of man, for there are camps in the arrangement of the Chariot called by the name "gate," and some called "ears," and some called "eyes," etc., and some further called "feet," and likewise all the other forms of the limbs in the constitution of man; and each of these supernal camps is the secret of that action to which the limb is compared, and all these camps, when joined together as one, are called "Adam," and they are all thrones for the great Name, blessed be He, and He, blessed be He, rules over all of them, and He is within them like the soul within the body, and from Him they receive their flow and their permanence - so far, in brief, his intent. Along these lines, Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Tikkunim (28a, 130a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:40: Along these lines, they explain in the Zohar (Toldot 134b) that the Torah, man, and the world are one matter - their words: "come and see, whoever occupies himself with Torah sustains the world and sustains every single deed in its proper repair, and there is no single limb standing in man that does not have its counterpart, a creature, in the world - for just as man is divided into limbs, all of which stand as levels arranged one over another, and when they are all properly arranged, they are one body - so too the world, all those creatures are limb after limb, standing one over another, and when they are all properly arranged, they too are truly one body. And all this is in the pattern of the Torah, for the Torah is entirely limbs and sections, standing one over another, and when they are all properly arranged, they become one body" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:41: Because we are not careful in our language to mention body and human form and the like, matters of body and physicality, above, and this matter is very far from being believed, since He, blessed be He, is not a body nor possessed of any shape, His throne and His garment should not be connected or termed with images of the body, God forbid; rather, all of these are only appellations for hidden matters, and concealed names, all of them holy names. Whoever has read Sefer Brit Menuchah will see something of this, that although he did not speak of Atzilut, he termed all the limbs with holy names, calling the Name of Seventy-two the lung, and the Name of Forty-two the liver, and likewise for all the other limbs.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:42: Along these lines, Rabbi Yosef Gikatilla writes in the introduction to Sefer HaOrah. He further writes in his commentary on the Chariot - his words: "and I tell you a general rule, and keep it always: do not let it enter your mind, wherever you find Me calling out toward the language of 'hand' or 'foot' or other limbs I have specified, that this means the form of a hand or the form of a foot, or the essence of a hand or the essence of a foot - for this is not so, neither a little nor a lot. Rather, the matter follows only the manner of naming, not the manner of essence and substance and form, since the forms of the Chariot are grasped only in supernal visions, by prophets and seers. Nevertheless, some ranks of angels are clothed in a garment close to human eyes, and this is a known matter regarding the powers of the garment; and know and believe that each of the joints of the Chariot, called hand and foot and ear and eye and the like - for all these there is an inner, supernal source, like a flowing spring, and it bestows upon each of the joints of the Chariot what it can sustain, each according to its kind and matter, so is its grasp and its receiving - how [is it that] this one's vision is not like that one's? And all is emanated upon them from the Name, blessed be He, in the secret of the ten sefirot, through which the intent and permanence of all existing things is completed; and these ten sefirot, in which is the place of all being in the world, no one can know their essence and matter, and they do not enter into any image or measure or knowledge of anything existing among all existing things - and so the prophet proclaims (Isaiah 40:25) 'and to whom will you liken Me, that I should be equal? says the Holy One'; and whoever sets in his mind that they have a boundary or a measure or an image is of little faith, like one who has no god, and worships his own reflection" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:43: In the words of this master, of blessed memory, there is enough to negate physicality from all things, since everything mentioned in the Torah and the Prophets, such as (Isaiah 34:6) "the sword of the Lord is full of blood," is all a parable. This is likewise explained in the portion of Shemot (Zohar 19b), on this verse - Rabbi Abba said: this sword is the judgment He carries out, as it is written (I Chronicles 21:16) "and David saw the angel of the Lord standing between heaven and earth, with a drawn sword in his hand" - and was there really a drawn sword in the angel's hand? Rather, permission was given [to him] to carry out judgment. If so, what is meant by "and he returned his sword to its sheath"? Rabbi Abba said, that judgment returned to the Master of Judgment, and permission to the One to whom permission belongs - so far, as relevant to us. And if in this matter our Sages, of blessed memory, stripped away physicality, how much more so in the very highest matters - rather, certainly everything mentioned in the Torah, "the eyes of the Lord," "the ears of the Lord," is all a parable for providence or for hearing.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:44: Along these lines, there is a second aspect concerning the world in general and its creatures, that they were all created from the four elements - this indicates that one Creator brought them into existence with His great Name, which has four letters, which are the root of the four elements, as is explained in the Tikkunim (68b), and we shall quote his words below.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:45: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains this matter (Zohar, Vaera 23b) - his words: "Rabbi Shimon said, come and see, there are four primordial ones, the secret of faith, the fathers of all worlds and the secret of the holy supernal Chariot, and they are fire, spirit [air], water, and earth. These are the supernal secret and the fathers of all worlds, the fathers of everything, and from them go forth gold, silver, copper, and iron, and beneath them are other metals resembling them, in the pattern of these. Come and see, fire, spirit, water, and earth - these are the primordial ones and the roots of above and below, and the lower and upper beings stand upon them, and these are the four corresponding to the four directions of the world, and they stand upon these four: north, south, east, west - these are the four directions of the world, and they stand upon these four: fire in the direction of north, spirit in the direction of east, water in the direction of south, earth in the direction of west; these four are bound to these four, and they are all one, and they make four metals, which are gold, silver, copper, and iron - here are twelve, and they are all one" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:46: When a person discerns this matter with his intellect, he will recognize his Creator from the side of His actions, whether from the side of the metals mentioned, or from the side of man himself, composed of the four elements, as explained there above. And from this one may also discern the secret of precious stones and pearls, some of which are white in color, whose property is grace and kindness, and some red in color, whose property is to instill dread - all coming from the supernal root of the supernal attributes.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:47: He further explains there that we find the north moist, with water, and the south hot and dry, and says that the Holy One, blessed be He, made this so as to bind the winds of the world one to another, just as the supernal attributes blend above, south in north and north in south, and so their matter below, in this world, that the waters, which are in the south, go to the north, and the fire of the north enters the south - this is the secret of the Binding of Isaac, explained in the Zohar in the explanation of that portion (Vayera 119b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:48: Further, concerning matters of the examination of the creation of the world, they elaborate in the Zohar (Vayikra 9b), and I have chosen to quote part of his words, not all, due to their length - his words: "Rabbi Yehudah opened, 'and God said, let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters' - come and see, at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created seven firmaments above, He created seven lands below, seven seas, seven rivers, seven days, seven weeks, seven years, seven times, seven thousand years is the duration of the world, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is in the seventh of everything."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:49: Seven heavens above, and in each and every one, stars and constellations and suns that serve in each and every firmament, and in all of them are chariots one over another, to accept upon themselves the yoke of the kingdom of their Master. And in all these firmaments are chariots and suns, differing one from another, one over another - some with six wings and some with four wings, some with four faces and some with two faces and some with one, and some are blazing fire, some water, some spirit, this is [the meaning of] (Psalms 104:4) "who makes His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire" - and all these firmaments, one over another, like layers of an onion, these below and these above, and each and every firmament goes and shakes from dread of its Master, upon His word they travel and upon His word they stand, and above all of them is the Holy One, blessed be He, who carries everything with His strength and might.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:50: In this pattern, seven lands below, all of them inhabited, except that some are above and some below, and the Land of Israel is above all, and Jerusalem is above all inhabited lands - and we, dwellers of the south, have seen in the earlier books, in the book of Adam, that all these lands are thus divided, all found below in the pattern of those firmaments above, one over another and one over another, and between each land and land is a firmament separating this from that, and therefore all the lands are separated by names, and between them are the Garden of Eden and Gehinnom, and among them are differing creatures, one from another, in the pattern of those chariots above, some with two faces and some with four and some with one, and the appearance of these is not like these, and if you say, etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:51: At the end they say - their words: Rabbi Nehora Sabba once traveled on the great sea, and the sea grew turbulent and all those on the boat were lost; a miracle was performed for him, and he descended by known paths into the heart of the sea, and went out from beneath the sea into an inhabited place, and saw creatures there, all of them small, praying a prayer, and he did not know what they were saying; a miracle was performed for him and he ascended. He said: happy are the righteous who occupy themselves with Torah and know the hidden supernal secrets; woe to those who dispute their words and do not believe. From that day, when he would come to the study house and say a matter of Torah, he would weep; they said to him, why do you weep? He said to them, because I once transgressed against the faith in the words of the Sages, and I fear the judgment of that world - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:52: When a person considers the creation of the world, its greatness, the great sea, and its creatures, as it is said (Psalms 104:25) "this sea, great and wide of hands, wherein are creeping things innumerable" - our Sages, of blessed memory, say (Mishnah, end of Kiddushin) that most sailors are pious, since they see the wonders of the Lord on the great sea, as it is written (Psalms 107:24) "these see the works of the Lord, and His wonders in the deep." And in what the Lord rebuked Job, saying to him (Job 38:16) "have you entered the springs of the sea, or walked in the recesses of the deep," etc., "have you comprehended the breadth of the earth? Tell Me, if you know it all" (ibid. 18), "have you entered the treasuries of snow" (ibid. 22), "who shakes the earth out of its place, and its pillars tremble" (ibid. 9:6) - which is the matter of earthquakes, one of the great signs showing the creation, and the reason for earthquakes is explained in the portion of Shemot (Zohar 17b), and the other particulars mentioned there - certainly he will recognize the greatness of the Creator and know that He created everything, that He created everything for His glory, and he will subject himself to His service and love Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:53: Among the particulars of examination is what Rabbi Yehudah mentions at the beginning of the passage we quoted, "He created seven firmaments," etc., "seven seas," etc., "and the Holy One, blessed be He, is in the seventh of everything," for the Holy One, blessed be He, chose the seventh things for Himself, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain in the midrash (Yalkut Shmuel, remez 94), and Rabbi Menachem Recanati, of blessed memory, quotes it in his commentary.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:54: It is fitting that a person discern this very matter, that it is found in the mouths of all the nations in seventy languages, that the name "Sabbath" has not changed in any language, but all call the seventh day Shabbat. The reason is that the Sabbath indicates the renewal of the world, and that the Holy One, blessed be He, created it in seven days and rested and kept Sabbath on the seventh, and therefore it has not changed, so that all recognize that there is one Creator of all. Of this kind of examination is the river Sambatyon, which flows all six days and rests on the seventh.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:55: Our Sages, of blessed memory, explain another proof for the Sabbath, in Midrash Tehillim, on the psalm (Psalms 19:2) "the heavens declare the glory of God," on the verse (Proverbs 16:4) "the Lord has made everything for his purpose" [le-ma'anehu] - he says, his words: "another interpretation, 'for its testimony' [read: le'edutо], along the lines of what is said (Exodus 20:13) 'you shall not bear false witness against your neighbor,' and it is written (Psalms 122:8) 'for the sake of my brothers and my friends' [related word]. Rabbi Abbahu said, there are two things the nations of the world do not deny concerning the Holy One, blessed be He: that He created the world in six days, and that He revives the dead. How so? A person goes and mounts [an animal] for riding all the days of the week, and it ascends [obeys], but on the Sabbath it does not ascend; and an animal, even on a weekday, does not ascend for one that is not destined to live in the future to come - hence, 'all the works of the Lord' are 'for His testimony'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:56: Further, concerning the matter of examination, is what the prophet says (Isaiah 40:26) "lift up your eyes on high and see who created these, who brings out their host by number, calling them all by name, who stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them out like a tent to dwell in." And in the Zohar (Bereishit 1b), Rashbi, peace be upon him, says that Elijah came and said to him, "Rabbi, do you know what 'who created these' [mi bara eleh] means?" I said to him, "these are the heavens and their hosts, the work of the Holy One, blessed be He, which a person must observe and bless Him for, as it is written (Psalms 8:4-2) 'when I see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers,' etc., 'O Lord, our Master, how mighty is Your Name in all the earth'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:57: Rashbi, peace be upon him (Zohar, Pekudei 231b), further explains this verse, and explains it more - his words: "rather, 'lift up your eyes on high' - whoever wishes to observe and know the works of the Holy One, blessed be He, should raise his eyes above and see how many hosts and how many camps of works, differing one from another, greater one than another, and then, when you see and ask and say, 'who created these' - 'who created these,' we have already established the secret of 'who created these,' that this place standing on high is hidden and concealed and unknown, and always stands ready to be asked, since that place is not revealed. 'Who brings out their host by number' - what is 'brings out'? Rather, because that place, hidden and concealed, brought out everything in the secret of the voice that issues from the shofar" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:58: Further on, he explains further that there is firmament and stars, one above another, down to when the matter descends to this firmament and these stars visible to our eyes - his words: "come and see, those stars below stand by a drawing drawn from the supernal secret, since everything stands in the supernal image, as has been established; so all those stars and constellations of the height of the firmament all stand to guide by them the world below, and from there they spread, until levels stand in those lower stars - for they all have no power at all of their own, as has been established, and they all stand under the authority of the One above - and therefore it is written (Isaiah 47:13) 'let now the astrologers, the stargazers stand up and save you' - and everything is under authority, as has been said" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:59: Although the plain sense of the verse "lift up your eyes on high," etc., "who brings out their host by number," concerns the creation of the heavens and the hosts of stars, which go out and enter by number and by name, nevertheless, there, in the Zohar (Bereishit 2b), he explains "Bereishit" as referring to Israel, who have six hundred thousand souls, and not one man is ever missing from six hundred thousand - this indicates that they are the counterpart of the supernal Chariot, which has six hundred thousand aspects, as is known to those who know wisdom. I likewise heard from the masters of astronomy that all the stars number six hundred thousand.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:60: There are further matters concerning examination: when one discerns the particular matters of the world, he will find them all hinting at supernal matters, and there is no need to elaborate on them. I further heard from my teacher, peace be upon him, a matter of examination comprising all herbs, seeds, and trees - that you will find that oil comes forth from all of them, and this indicates the secret of wisdom spreading through all created things, as it says (Psalms 104:24) "You made them all with wisdom." So too one should observe the matter of thunder, which our Sages, of blessed memory, explain, on the verse (Ecclesiastes 3:14) "and God has done it so that men should fear before Him," that they were created only to straighten out the crookedness of the heart, and we quoted this in the Gate of Fear, chapter 11. And likewise several other things, like earthquakes and the roar of the lion, etc., see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:61: The pious author of Chovot HaLevavot writes (Gate of Self-Reckoning, chapter 3) that one must examine all the things in the world, such as the eternal motion of the spheres, the flowing of rivers of water from springs, night and day without rest or ceasing, the descent of rains, the blowing of winds, and the emergence of the child from the womb - all these indicate the wonders of the Creator, His mercy, and His abundant providence over His creatures, and one who neglects to observe these matters is like one who is blind; therefore one must open the eyes of his intellect to examine things, in order to observe and know the wonders of the Lord. This is a summary of his intent, and he elaborates further; whoever wishes to see it, the book is before him, let him examine it there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:62: Among the things one must discern in the matter of the creation, in the workings of the world, is by observing the workings of day and night, which is one of the things created in the account of Creation, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain; and it is known that the measure of day and the measure of night have their secret above, in Atzilut, being the governance of judgment and the governance of mercy. Therefore David the king, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 104:20-22) "You appoint darkness and it is night, in which all the beasts of the forest creep forth; the young lions roar for prey and seek their food from God" - and our Sages, of blessed memory, say that this pertains to the attribute of night, as Rashbi explains in the portion of Bemidbar (119b), on the matter of (Psalms 7:12) "and God is angry every day" - and this is because the attribute of night sustains these spirits that it needs for the repair of the world, along the lines of (Genesis 29:3) "and they would put the stone back over the mouth of the well," as is explained in the portion of Vayetze (Zohar 152a).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:63: It says, "when the sun rises, they gather themselves," because then the governance of mercy rules, and all those powers enter into the hole of the great deep, as is explained in the Zohar in several places, and support for this is (Genesis 44:3) "as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys." This matter is perceptible even to the senses, in the matter of the sick, for at night their illness weighs heavier upon them, and by day, especially until midday, the illness eases, since then Chesed rules.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 5:64: This is what the verse says (Deuteronomy 4:39) "and you shall know this day and take it to your heart, that the Lord, He is God" - meaning, when you know the secret of the "day," that "day" unqualified is day and night, as it says (Genesis 1:5) "and there was evening and there was morning, one day," in the whole account of Creation - you shall know that the Lord, He is God, which are the governance of mercy, the secret of YHVH, and the governance of judgment, in the secret of Elohim - both a single unity, just as it is impossible for night without day, or day without night.
